components.sublabel: RETAIN · full hash, scope and coverage

boundaries.label: Trusted worker — evidence preparation and response validation

cards.title: The LLM judges; the server protects the boundary
items: The judge decides PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE for each frozen criterion and supplies a concise finding with real evidence references.

Server code keeps authentication, cleanup, full evidence integrity, schema/reference checks, cancellation, deadline and immutable receipt rules. It does not replace the judge verdict with the old threshold evaluator.

cards.title: P17.5 criteria become a published rubric
items: Each criterion needs requirement, passWhen, failWhen, inconclusiveWhen and required evidence, plus explicit scope, units and clock. AI suggestions remain human-reviewed before publication.
New canonical rubric/evaluator versions preserve historical synthetic digests, prior evaluator1 decisions and receipt replay. Initial check kinds remain unchanged.

cards.title: Failures and retries stay distinct
items: Missing or invalid required evidence cannot produce PASS. Refusal or model/provider outage is not a failed behavior criterion.

Bounded transient provider retries reuse the same packet, prompt and model settings. Never retry a FAIL to obtain a nicer answer; never rerun the simulation. A provider timeout can cause another billed request unless provider idempotency is established.

cards.title: Proposal status and explicit limits
items: Conceptual design revision for the locally implemented, uncommitted P17 baseline; this is not a code-at-HEAD or deployed-system inventory. RETAIN means keep that approved baseline responsibility.
Prompt draft: docs/architecture/proposals/llm-judge-system-prompt.md. Provider/model and outbound evidence policy remain unconfigured. No model calls, credentials or paid checks performed.
Proposed visible stages: Validate evidence → Prepare packet → LLM judge → Validate response → Commit. Raw binary ULog and unknown PX4 boot/clock facts are not magically understood by a text judge.
